sections.heading: Alarm path: broadband first, cellular mid-incident
text: Battery sensors talk to a mains-powered base station over a proprietary sub-GHz radio; the base station runs the certified alarm state machine locally and signals the monitoring center over broadband first, failing over to a built-in cellular modem under active supervision — mid-incident if necessary, with sequence numbers preserved so the monitoring side never double-books or loses an event.
bullets: **Glassbreak sensor GB-2** hears a break and sends a sub-GHz alarm frame to **Ember-M0**.
**Ember-M0** latches ALARM in the state machine, fires the siren, and hands the event to **Hearth-A53**.
**Hearth-A53** sends signal `seq 4181` (alarm, zone 3) to **Hearthgate** over broadband TLS, and Hearthgate acks it within 2 seconds.
Hearthgate appends the event to **Register** and forwards it to **Overwatch**, which opens incident `INC-7731`.
Hearth-A53 sends `seq 4182` (siren-on) into a broadband link that has just died, so no ack returns.
The 15-second ack supervision timer expires, so Hearth-A53 powers the LTE modem and opens a TLS session to Hearthgate over the cellular APN.
Hearth-A53 retransmits `seq 4182` and continues with `seq 4183` on the cellular path, and Hearthgate dedupes on `(account, seq)` so nothing double-books.
Overwatch assigns the incident to an agent, and the monitoring-center acknowledgment travels back to the panel over the same cellular session.
Ember-M0 marks the incident center-acknowledged, the keypad shows `MONITORING NOTIFIED`, and Hearth-A53 keeps probing broadband for fail-back.
*Failure mode — broadband drops*: the 15-second ack supervision above triggers cellular failover mid-incident; sequence numbering (the `(account, seq)` dedupe) makes the switch invisible to Register.

*Failure mode — both uplinks down*: the siren and latched alarm state still work locally; events queue in Ember-M0 flash with their seq numbers and flush in order on restore, and Hearthgate gap detection reconciles against Register.

sections.heading: Camera-verified dispatch
text: Monitored plans add camera verification: an agent reviews the attached clip, attempts a talk-down through the camera's speaker, and only then decides on dispatch.
bullets: On the ALARM latch, **Hearth-A53** asks **Sentry Cam** to record, and the camera uploads a 30-second clip to **Clipline** over wifi.
Clipline attaches the clip to `INC-7731` and tells **Overwatch** the incident is camera-verification eligible.
Overwatch pops the incident on a **Guardline** agent console with the clip queued first.
The agent reviews the clip and confirms a person inside the premises perimeter.
The agent opens a talk-down: Guardline relays live agent audio to the camera's speaker while the camera streams live video back.
The subject does not leave, so the agent marks the incident "verified intruder" and requests dispatch from Overwatch.
Overwatch hands the dispatch request and clip reference to **Summons**, which forwards it to the regional emergency-services gateway — verified video raises response priority.
**Beacon** pushes the owner the full timeline: alarm, clip, talk-down attempted, dispatch requested.

sections.heading: Walk test: every sensor exercised
text: The owner walk-tests the whole sensor inventory from the app, with dispatch suppressed for the duration and a signed record kept at the end.
bullets: The owner starts a walk test in the app; the request lands on **Roster**, which commands the panel into TEST mode.
**Ember-M0** enters TEST: sensors report normally, the siren stays quiet, and every signal is tagged test-mode; **Overwatch** marks the account "test in progress — suppress dispatch."
The owner trips each sensor in turn, and each sub-GHz frame reaches Ember-M0, which chirps the keypad and marks that sensor tested.
**Hearth-A53** streams per-sensor results to Roster, which updates the walk-test inventory: front entry PASS, hall motion PASS.
The basement entry sensor never reports; after two attempts Roster shows it FAIL (last supervisory 3 days ago, battery critical).
The owner swaps the sensor battery and trips it again, and the arriving frame flips basement entry to PASS.
The owner ends the test at the keypad, and Ember-M0 verifies every enrolled sensor was exercised before leaving TEST.
Hearth-A53 sends the test-complete report to Hearthgate, which tells Overwatch to lift dispatch suppression.
Roster stores the signed walk-test record and the panel returns to DISARMED/READY — fully armed-capable.
*Failure mode — sensor battery low*: supervisory frames carry `batt_mv`; Roster schedules a keypad chirp and app nag; a sensor silent past 3 supervisory windows is flagged unsupervised.
*Failure mode — walk test abandoned*: TEST auto-expires after 60 minutes and suppression lifts even if the app session died; the keypad exit above is explicit, expiry is the backstop.

sections.heading: Duress disarm: identical locally, silent upstream
text: The keypad supports a duress code that looks exactly like a normal disarm at the premises while silently opening a priority incident upstream.
bullets: The front door opens while armed-away; the entry sensor's frame reaches Ember-M0, which starts the 30-second entry delay and beeps the keypad.
Hearth-A53 sends a pending-entry event to Hearthgate so the monitoring side has context if the delay expires.
The user keys a 4-digit code, and the keypad sends it to Ember-M0 in a rolling-code envelope.
Normal path: the code matches the owner's code, Ember-M0 disarms and cancels the delay, and Overwatch closes the pending entry silently on the disarm event.
Duress path: the code matches the owner's duress code, and locally everything is identical — the keypad shows DISARMED, no siren, entry delay cancelled.
The disarm event Hearth-A53 sends carries `flags.duress=1` inside the signed envelope, invisible at the premises.
Overwatch opens a silent duress incident and routes it to an agent flagged NO PREMISES CONTACT — no callback, no siren, no talk-down.
Beacon suppresses the normal owner push, because an attacker watching the owner's phone must see nothing unusual.
The agent follows the duress protocol and requests priority dispatch through Summons while the panel continues to look disarmed.

**[Countersign](https://github.com/hearthline/monitor-core/blob/main/countersign/codes.go#L57)** owns the keypad code policy behind this — auth, panel client certificates, agent SSO, and *per-account duress codes* — which is why the duress code can look exactly like a normal disarm at the premises.
*The argument*: `pst` (Ember-M0's local state) and `kd` (what the keypad shows) end **identically** on both paths — only `mlog` (the monitoring side) diverges.

Overwatch opens a silent incident: NO PREMISES CONTACT
Owner push suppressed by duress policy
Agent requests priority dispatch; panel still looks disarmed

sections.heading: Failure modes: power, region, and load
text: Failure modes that don't interrupt any of the three boards above but shape how the panel behaves under power loss, backend region loss, and monitoring-center load.
bullets: **Power fails**: 24 h on the backup pack; Hearth-A53 sheds wifi and camera liaison while Ember-M0 keeps the state machine, sub-GHz, and on-demand LTE alive; the keypad announces "on backup power."
**Hearthgate region down**: panels retry the alternate region endpoint (DNS-steered).
**Agent overload**: Overwatch queues incidents against SLA clocks; alarm events are never dropped, but camera verification degrades to the unverified dispatch policy.
